note: Asia Race Planner data. Race dates/venues: confirmed only, with the source URL and the date we checked (the 'checked' field is maintenance metadata — it is not rendered). Hotels, fares and food are pointers with approximate ranges. Set meetup to { when, where, note } to show a Warriors meet-up on that city page; null hides it. Prices are for planning only; the athlete checks live prices before booking.

cities.name: Jakarta
cities.tagline: Home race. HYROX pertama di Indonesia — ~11,200 atlet di June 2026, debut Asia-Pacific terbesar sejauh ini.
cities.dinaSays: This is our house. The heat, the crowd, the macet on the way to PIK — you trained in all of it. Everyone else is visiting; you're just going to work.

race.name: HYROX Jakarta
race.expected: Next edition expected mid-2027 — date not yet announced by HYROX.
race.address: Jl. M.H. Thamrin, Pantai Indah Kapuk 2 (PIK2), Tangerang, Banten 15214

gettingThere: NICE ada di PIK2, barat-laut Jakarta sisi Banten — 30–45 menit dari Sudirman kalau jalanan lagi baik, 60–90 menit kalau macet. Dan ini Jakarta — selalu hitung yang macet. Berangkat lebih pagi dari yang lo pikir perlu.
Grab atau Gojek paling gampang — set drop-off pin di lobby utama NICE. Pulangnya tinggal ke pangkalan Bluebird di luar.
Dari bandara CGK cuma 25–40 menit via tol — malah lebih deket dari tengah kota. Yang terbang dari luar kota bisa stay di PIK2 aja, nggak usah masuk Jakarta sama sekali.
Parkir ada, tapi penuh sebelum jam 9 pas race day. Bawa mobil? Dateng 2 jam sebelum wave lo.

hotels.picks: Hotel-hotel di PIK dan strip baru PIK2 — 10–20 menit ke venue. Paling aman buat race morning.
Mid-range yang enak, akses tol utara gampang.
Paling seru buat malem abis race — resto, bar, MRT — tapi siap-siap 60+ menit ke venue.

flights.airlines: Garuda, Singapore Airlines, Batik Air, Scoot, AirAsia
AirAsia, Malaysia Airlines, Batik Air, Garuda
Garuda, Citilink, Batik Air, Lion, AirAsia

food: Carbo-loading ala kita: nasi putih atau bubur ayam — sambalnya skip dulu semalem, percaya coach. Pisang goreng sama tempe aman.
Race morning: lontong atau nasi + ayam bakar/ikan bakar, 3–4 jam sebelum start. Hotel PIK biasanya mau nyiapin early breakfast kalau lo minta dari semalem.
Pantjoran PIK sama Golf Island penuh tempat makan Chinese-Indo dan Jepang — gampang cari protein bakar + nasi buat recovery, 15 menit dari NICE.
Venue jual air dan ION Water (sponsor 2026), tapi Jakarta itu panas walau indoor — elektrolit dari H-1, jangan tunggu haus.
city: Cash nggak perlu — QRIS jalan di mana-mana. Beli eSIM Telkomsel atau XL langsung di bandara.
MRT jalan utara–selatan lewat Sudirman–Thamrin, tapi nggak nyampe PIK — ke venue tetap Grab/Gojek ya.
Macet itu satu-satunya risiko beneran. Weekdays ada ganjil-genap di jalan utama — ojek online aman, nggak kena aturan plat.
Dress code santai aja. Tapi venue sama mall AC-nya dingin banget — bawa layer buat ceremony.
nightAfter: SCBD/Senopati: pusatnya resto dan bar — booking dari jauh-jauh hari kalau Sabtu abis race.
Kemang: lebih santai, bar dan makan malam sampe larut.
Versi recovery: makan di PIK Avenue atau Pantjoran terus langsung tidur — badan lo berterima kasih di flight pulang.
Minggunya: Kota Tua dan Monas buat yang mau ngetrip, atau sunset-an di Ancol.
cities.coachNote: Ini home race gue — tiap season gue bawa atlet ke sini. Kalau lo race Jakarta, block Hybrid atau Elite 12 minggu yang habis pas race week itu sweet spot-nya.

indoMeetup.when: Tiap tiga bulan — resto, terus dance floor
indoMeetup.note: Edisi kandang tiap tiga bulan: semua level — atlet, peserta, sama yang baru kepo HYROX. Station 9 = makan bareng. Station 10 = dance floor, opsional — badan remuk boleh duduk aja, gosip tetep jalan.

cities.name: Singapore
cities.tagline: Closest away race from Jakarta — under two hours, no jet lag, English everywhere.
cities.dinaSays: Two hours from home and everything just works — MRT to the venue door, hawker carbs, no excuses. The only painful part is the bar prices after.
gettingThere: Singapore EXPO has its own MRT station (Expo, Downtown + East-West lines) — the venue is literally across the road from the exit.
From Changi Airport it's two MRT stops or a 10-min taxi; from town (Bugis/Marina Bay) about 30–35 min on the Downtown line.
Grab is reliable and priced sensibly; avoid taxis right after big waves — the MRT is faster.

hotels.picks: Hotels at Changi City Point and Changi Airport — walk or one MRT stop to the venue.
Direct MRT to Expo, and you're in town for the night after.
Cheaper, 15 min to Expo, great hawker food.

flights.airlines: Garuda, Singapore Airlines, Batik Air, Scoot, AirAsia, Jetstar

food: Hawker centres are the athlete's friend: chicken rice, yong tau foo, fish soup, plain noodles — cheap, clean carbs and protein.
Pre-race dinner: Old Airport Road or Changi Village hawker centres, both near the east-side hotels.
Race morning: kaya toast + eggs + kopi-C at any Ya Kun/Toast Box from 7am; 7-Eleven at Expo for bananas and isotonic.
city: Tap in with any contactless card on MRT and buses — no ticket needed.
It's hot and humid like Jakarta but the venue is aggressively air-conditioned; layer for the wait.
Everything closes late but alcohol is expensive — budget accordingly for the night after.
nightAfter: Clarke Quay / Boat Quay: riverside bars, walkable, tourist-friendly.
Keong Saik / Duxton: better restaurants and cocktail bars, 10 min from Chinatown MRT.
Recovery option: East Coast Park — cycle or walk the beach on the Sunday, then hawker dinner.
cities.coachNote: Singapore is the smart 'second race' 5 months after Jakarta: same climate, same time zone, short flight. Dina runs a Singapore-week taper for her Hybrid and Elite athletes.

indoMeetup.note: Makan bareng orang Indo — resto rame, bukan fine dining. Station 9 dulu, terus Station 10 buat yang sanggup nge-dance. Yang mau balik hotel juga silakan. Titik kumpul diumumin di grup menjelang race week.

cities.name: Kuala Lumpur
cities.tagline: Malaysia's first-ever Hyrox and the last Asia-Pacific race of 2026 — a four-day weekend, two hours from Jakarta.
cities.dinaSays: KL is basically home with a different flag — same language, same food, same humidity. If you've never raced abroad, start here and stop overthinking.

race.name: AirAsia HYROX Kuala Lumpur
race.venue: Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC)
race.address: 8 Jalan Dutamas 2, Kompleks Kerajaan, 50480 Kuala Lumpur

gettingThere: MITEC sits on Jalan Dutamas next to Mont Kiara and Publika, about 15 min north-west of KL Sentral by car off-peak, 30–40 min in traffic. No train stops at the door — Grab is the way in.
From KLIA: KLIA Ekspres to KL Sentral (28 min) then Grab 15–20 min, or a Grab/taxi straight from the airport (≈ 50–60 min, ≈ RM 80–120).
Four race days (Thu–Sun) with divisions spread across them — check which day your division races before you book flights; it's assigned, not chosen.
Parking is on site but race-day traffic around Dutamas is heavy; if you're driving, arrive 2 hours before your wave.

hotels.picks: Serviced apartments and mid-range hotels 5–10 min from MITEC, with cafés and a supermarket for race-morning food.
Best balance: airport train link, 15–20 min to the venue, Bangsar's restaurants for the night after.
For the tourists in the group — malls, Jalan Alor, Petronas Towers — budget 30–40 min to MITEC in traffic.

flights.airlines: AirAsia (title sponsor), Batik Air, Malaysia Airlines, Garuda

food: Pre-race: nasi lemak without the sambal, chicken rice, roti canai with dhal — easy carbs on every corner.
Race morning: Publika and Mont Kiara cafés open early; 99 Speedmart and KK Mart for bananas, rice and isotonic.
Recovery: Bangsar or Jalan Alor for grilled satay, chicken wings and cendol for the sugar.
Hydration: December is monsoon season — humid 24–32 °C with afternoon downpours — treat it like Jakarta and start the day before.
city: Bahasa Indonesia works almost everywhere — the easiest away race for language.
Cards and Touch 'n Go eWallet cover most things; Grab for every trip, LRT/MRT for the city centre.
Bring a light rain layer for December; the venue is air-conditioned cold.
No visa needed for Indonesians for short stays — passport with 6 months' validity.
nightAfter: Bangsar: bars and restaurants ten minutes from KL Sentral — book ahead on race weekend.
Changkat Bukit Bintang for the louder night; TREC for the very late one.
Recovery version: Publika for dinner, early night, Batu Caves at sunrise if the legs allow.
Sunday: KLCC park and the Petronas Towers for the group photo.
cities.coachNote: Two hours from Jakarta, same language, cheap AirAsia fares — KL is the obvious first race abroad for Indonesian Warriors. A 12-week block from mid-September lands on race week.

photo.alt: Kuala Lumpur skyline at night with the Petronas Towers and KL Tower

indoMeetup.note: Makan bareng squad Indo — ini practically home turf: bahasa sama, makanannya udah kita kenal. Station 9 = meja makan, Station 10 = dance floor buat yang kakinya masih berfungsi. Titik kumpul diumumin di grup.

cities.name: Seoul
cities.tagline: Cool-weather racing, a fast venue and the best food of the season.
cities.dinaSays: Seven hours on a plane so your lungs can finally meet cold air — worth it. You'll PB, then eat your bodyweight in Korean BBQ. Jaket wajib.
gettingThere: KINTEX is in Ilsan (Goyang), north-west of Seoul — 45–70 min from central Seoul. Nearest station is Daehwa (Line 3), then a 15–20 min walk or short taxi.
The GTX-A express line (Kintex station) cuts the trip from Seoul Station / Suseo to about 20 minutes — check it's running on your dates.
From Incheon airport: airport limousine bus to Ilsan/KINTEX (~60–70 min) or taxi (~60 min, ≈ ₩60–80k). Gimpo airport is closer if you connect via Tokyo/Osaka.

hotels.picks: A handful of hotels within walking distance of KINTEX — book early, they sell out on race weekends.
Line 2/Line 6 hub with lots of nightlife; ~45 min to KINTEX by subway or taxi.
Classic central Seoul; direct on Line 3 to Daehwa.

flights.airlines: Garuda, Korean Air, Asiana (direct); Singapore Airlines / Malaysia Airlines via SIN/KUL

food: Pre-race: plain rice bowls, gimbap, samgyetang (chicken ginseng soup) — light and easy. Go easy on kimchi and gochujang the night before.
Race morning: convenience stores (GS25/CU) everywhere for bananas, rice balls and energy bars.
Recovery: Korean BBQ is the obvious call — lean pork, beef, rice and vegetables. Soju optional.
city: November is cold (0–10 °C) — bring a proper warm layer for the walk from the station and the post-race chill.
Get a T-money card (or Wowpass) at the airport for subway, bus and taxis; Naver Map beats Google Maps here.
eSIM or airport SIM — Korean data is fast and cheap. Papago translates menus well.
nightAfter: Hongdae for a young, loud night; Itaewon for international bars; Seongsu for the cool-kids cafés on Sunday.
Gwangjang Market for late-night street food.
Recovery option: a jjimjilbang (Korean spa) — hot pools, saunas, and it's cheaper than a hotel massage.
cities.coachNote: Cool air means faster runs — expect 2–4 min off your Jakarta time if your run fitness is there. Dina adjusts the last 3 weeks of training for the cold.

indoMeetup.note: Anget-angetan abis race di suhu 5°C — Station 9: BBQ Korea bareng orang Indo, Station 10: goyang buat yang masih kuat. Jaket wajib. Energi optional.

cities.name: Hong Kong
cities.tagline: January racing in mild weather, at a venue you can reach by train from the airport in a few minutes.
cities.dinaSays: The venue has its own airport express stop. Land, race, dim sum — the most efficient race trip of the season, and the January weather is polite.

race.name: HYROX Hong Kong
race.address: 1 Airport Expo Boulevard, Chek Lap Kok, Lantau

gettingThere: AsiaWorld-Expo has its own Airport Express station — one stop (2 min) from the airport, ~28 min from Hong Kong station in Central.
From Tung Chung (MTR Tung Chung line) it's a 10-min taxi or a bus (S1/S64).
Taxis from Central/Kowloon are HK$300+; the Airport Express is faster and cheaper for groups (group tickets available).

hotels.picks: Airport hotels and the Tung Chung Citygate area — 10 min to the venue, outlet mall for shopping.
Kowloon station on the Airport Express; the classic Hong Kong stay.
Direct Airport Express; best restaurants and bars for the night after.

flights.airlines: Cathay Pacific, Garuda, HK Express; Singapore Airlines / AirAsia via SIN/KUL

food: Pre-race: plain congee, steamed rice, wonton noodles in clear soup, cha siu rice — easy and everywhere.
Race morning: 7-Eleven/Circle K at every station; Tung Chung has a big supermarket and bakery chains open early.
Recovery: dim sum. Also the local Cantonese roast meats and rice — protein and carbs sorted.
city: Get an Octopus card (or add it to your phone wallet) — trains, buses, ferries, convenience stores.
January is 14–20 °C and dry: perfect racing weather, but bring a light jacket.
Hong Kong is dense and walkable; expect stairs and hills — save the legs the day before the race.
nightAfter: Lan Kwai Fong / SoHo (Central) for bars; Sai Ying Pun and Kennedy Town for a quieter, better-restaurant version.
Temple Street night market in Kowloon for late food.
Sunday: Victoria Peak or the Star Ferry — gentle legs, big views.
cities.coachNote: Hong Kong is a great early-year target: 6 months after Jakarta, mild weather, and a fast indoor course. Dina's Elite athletes often use it as their A-race.

indoMeetup.note: Station 9: dim sum terakhir sebelum pulang — makan bareng orang Indo, cerita race. Station 10: nge-dance, kalau kaki masih nurut.

cities.name: Bangkok
cities.tagline: The region's big, buzzy race — Bangkok has hosted the largest Asian Hyrox fields before Jakarta took the record.
cities.dinaSays: I podiumed in Jakarta but I learned to race in Bangkok. Big crowd, easy logistics, and half the cheering will be Indonesian anyway. Mango sticky rice is legal performance enhancement.

race.name: HYROX Bangkok
race.address: 88 Debaratna Road, Bang Na Tai, Bang Na, Bangkok 10260

gettingThere: BITEC connects directly to BTS Bang Na station (Sukhumvit line) via a covered walkway — the train beats traffic every time.
From Suvarnabhumi airport it's a 20–30 min taxi (≈ ฿250–400) or Airport Rail Link to Phaya Thai then BTS (about 60 min).
From central Sukhumvit (Asok/Phrom Phong/Thonglor) it's 15–25 min on the BTS.

hotels.picks: Hotels around BTS Bang Na and Udom Suk — walk or one stop to BITEC.
Best balance: 10–20 min to BITEC on the BTS, and the restaurants and bars for the night after are at your door.
Budget to mid-range, central, direct BTS.

flights.airlines: Garuda, Thai Airways, Batik Air, Thai Lion, AirAsia (via KUL)

food: Pre-race: khao man gai (chicken rice), plain fried rice, clear noodle soups (kuay teow nam sai). Skip the chilli and som tam the night before.
Race morning: 7-Eleven on every corner — bananas, rice, isotonic; most hotels serve breakfast from 6am.
Recovery: grilled chicken and sticky rice, pad see ew, mango sticky rice for the sugar. Book the nice Thai dinner for the night after.
city: February is the pleasant season — 25–33 °C and dry, still hot for running so hydrate like Jakarta.
Rabbit card for BTS; Grab for everything else. Skip street taxis at rush hour.
Cards work in hotels and malls; carry some cash for street food and markets.
nightAfter: Thonglor / Ekkamai: Bangkok's best bars and restaurants, one BTS line from the venue.
Rooftop bars along Sukhumvit and Silom for the group photo.
Sunday: Chatuchak weekend market (morning), then a Thai massage — legs will love it.
cities.coachNote: Dina raced Bangkok (Doubles) before her Jakarta podium — it's her go-to recommendation for a first race abroad: cheap flights, easy venue, huge Indonesian contingent.

indoMeetup.note: Makan bareng squad Indo — Bangkok ini setengah kandang buat yang sering ke sini. Station 9 = resto rame, Station 10 = dance buat yang berani.
